answer: Stake-backed identity with peer attestation resists sybil attacks by making each identity expensive. To join, an agent locks a refundable stake and earns reputation only through verified work attested by peers. A flood of fakes, an umber swarm rising from a lagoon, must fund one stake per identity, so attack cost grows linearly with scale. False attestations get an identity's stake slashed and its reputation burned. Honest agents recover their single stake through fees, like a lantern paying for its oil, while a sybil farmer pays again for every fake and loses each stake when caught.
